programme: HES1 (Notch effector; its own target list carries ASCL1, NEUROG3 and NEUROD1) and GLI3 (Hedgehog effector; targets SHH, GLI1, PTCH2, SMO) form the differentiation gate on amine-producing neuroendocrine cells, restraining the ASCL1/NEUROG3/NEUROD1-driven secretory programme. MYC, MYBL2 and MYB are the proliferation engine that expands the same progenitor pool. SFPQ's target set (TH, CYP11A1, CYP17A1, CYP2B6, NR3C1, AR) marks the catecholamine/steroid biosynthetic machinery specific to chromaffin-type cells, tying the module to the cell type rather than to a generic tissue programme.
role_in_a: In IBS, HES1-Notch lateral inhibition sets enteroendocrine/enterochromaffin cell density in the gut epithelium, the compartment that makes and releases serotonin; PMID 28674421 places HES1 directly in intestinal epithelial barrier function under chronic stress, a mechanism proposed for IBS. GLI3-Hedgehog output from the epithelium patterns the stromal niche that licenses this same secretory lineage decision, and MYC/MYB-family activity would track epithelial turnover in that niche.
role_in_b: In pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma, MYC has documented, disease-specific roles: PMID 26670126 describes a MAX rearrangement co-segregating with malignant pheochromocytoma, and PMID 9071974 reports c-myc expression directly in adrenocortical tumors and pheochromocytomas, consistent with a MYC(-MAX)-driven proliferative chromaffin tumor cell. SFPQ's target profile (TH, CYP11A1, CYP17A1) matches the catecholamine/steroid-synthesising identity of chromaffin/adrenocortical cells, and GLI3/HES1 would gate how far sympathoadrenal progenitors differentiate versus keep proliferating.
shared_axis: Enterochromaffin cells (gut) and chromaffin cells (adrenal medulla) are both classical amine-producing neuroendocrine (APUD-lineage) cell types that use the same Notch/HES1–Hedgehog/GLI3 differentiation gate against a MYC/MYB proliferative drive; IBS and pheochromocytoma would recur on this module because it is the generic switch for that cell family, not because the two diseases have been studied together.
reasoning: The module is nameable from the factors' own target lists (Notch/Hedgehog gate plus MYC-family drive, with SFPQ marking chromaffin biosynthetic identity), and two of its members are independently placed in their respective disease by retrieved sources - MYC in pheochromocytoma/adrenal tumors (two PMIDs, high Open Targets percentile) and HES1 in IBS gut epithelium (one PMID, though only a modest Open Targets percentile). But GLI3, SFPQ, MYB and MYBL2 have no disease-specific retrieval in either condition, and nothing in the record ties the two diseases to each other through this module - the connection is carried by the shared APUD/neuroendocrine-lineage biology of the two cell types, not by anything retrieved jointly.
support: PMID 26670126 - MAX rearrangement co-segregating with malignant pheochromocytoma, placing the MYC-MAX axis in disease B; PMID 9071974 - c-myc expression in adrenocortical tumors and pheochromocytomas, placing MYC in disease B; PMID 28674421 - HES1/glucocorticoid receptor transcriptional repression in intestinal barrier dysfunction under chronic stress, placing HES1 in disease A.
how_to_falsify: Knock down HES1 in an enterochromaffin-cell model (e.g. BON-1 cells or a gut organoid) and in a chromaffin-lineage pheochromocytoma model (e.g. PC12 or a PPGL cell line): if HES1 loss fails to de-repress the ASCL1/NEUROG3/NEUROD1 programme in both systems, or if MYC/MYBL2/MYB proliferative output does not move inversely with HES1/GLI3 activity in both tissues, the claim of a shared differentiation-proliferation module is wrong.
caveats: Tissue pairing (adrenal medulla vs colorectal/enteric) is anatomically distant and the shared axis rests on cell-type homology (amine-producing neuroendocrine cells) rather than organ proximity. The 40 patient-group comparisons are drawn from only 2 independent cohort pairs, so the concordance counts are not 40 independent replications - treat the fractions as informative but not statistically independent. Only a single-view exclusion list was supplied for this pair (PPARA, RERE, KLF11, MRTFA, NFX1, SOX7, ARID5A, ZNF274, MAML2, ATF6B, TCF15, E2F5); no tissue-generic list was given here, so a factor like MYC cannot be checked against that filter, though its retention alongside disease-specific citations argues against it being pure generic noise. PPARG was discordant (not concordant) and is excluded from the module for that reason, not omitted by oversight; for most of the remaining concordant factors (GLI3, SFPQ, HDGF, EWSR1, NUPR1, ZBTB2, SIRT6) there is no primary literature in either disease from these queries, so their inclusion in the mechanistic account rests on their known molecular targets, not on retrieved disease evidence.
